page: Amazon Web Services mac2-m1ultra.metal is a bare-metal instance based on Apple Silicon arm64 architecture, classified within the General Purpose family. The server provides dedicated hardware access featuring 20 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz with 1 thread per core, delivering 20 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory, which provides 6.4 GB of RAM per core without hyperthreading overhead.

The hardware configuration includes no discrete GPU accelerators and offers no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data. Baseline network throughput is rated at 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

In terms of resource density, the combination of 20 physical Apple Silicon cores and 128.0 GB of memory yields a balance between compute throughput and memory allocation. The dedicated bare-metal model avoids hypervisor interference, though the absence of local disks necessitates reliance on networked volumes for disk-intensive pipelines.

This instance profile is oriented toward native Apple Silicon build pipelines, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) environments for macOS and iOS ecosystems, multi-threaded software compilation, and large-scale testing workloads requiring dedicated Apple hardware resources.
